questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close to another car's rear bumper):

options.text: Can anger other drivers.
Cannot result in a traffic ticket.
Reduces crashes by preventing being cut off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can anger other drivers.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is unsafe and can cause aggressive driving. Drivers can receive a ticket for unsafe driving.

questions.question: If you have an argument and are angry, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Drive on the interstate to feel better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions affect your driving ability. If you are angry, upset, worried, or scared, wait until you calm down before driving. You need to focus on the road without thinking about what upset you.

questions.question: If you meet an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Challenge them.
Stay out of their way.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of their way.
questions.explanation: All drivers must respect each other and follow the rules to prevent crashes. When you meet an aggressive driver, the safest choice is to stay out of their way. Do not compete with other drivers.

questions.question: Blind spots are:

options.text: Areas in your vision when you get tired.
Road areas you cannot see in your mirrors.
Traffic control signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road areas you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Check the areas near the rear corners of your vehicle. These areas are called blind spots because your mirrors cannot show them.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug and drink alcohol?

options.text: Nothing will happen.
You will be more alert.
You may not be safe to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not be safe to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving ability. They are especially dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: When you see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Go 15 mph if no children are visible.
Drive at normal speed but watch for children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely when you see a school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm. Stay stopped until the arm goes back and the bus starts moving. This applies whether you are going the same direction or opposite direction as the bus.

questions.question: Vehicles must have liability insurance:

options.text: Only on interstates.
Only when a minor is driving.
At all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: South Dakota law requires all vehicles to be registered and insured at all times. You must keep proof of insurance in your vehicle.

questions.question: You should drive at the maximum posted speed limit only:

options.text: At night.
During the day.
When conditions are perfect.

questions.correctAnswerText: When conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally go in ideal conditions. Drive at the same speed as other traffic, but not faster than the speed limit. All drivers share the responsibility of driving safely.

questions.question: Temporary signs in construction and work zones:

options.text: Have a red background with green lettering.
Have an orange background with black lettering.
Have a yellow background with blue lettering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have an orange background with black lettering.
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have orange backgrounds with black lettering and symbols.

questions.question: At a crosswalk:

options.text: You must let pedestrians cross.
Pedestrians must let you go.
Construction workers must let you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must let pedestrians cross.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crossings but must follow traffic signals. When there is no traffic signal, you must stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk, whether it is marked or not.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Flagger ahead.
Turn left at the intersection.
Last turn before a toll road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs mean there is work zone activity ahead. When you see orange signs, cones, or barrels, stay alert. A flagger ahead will direct traffic, and you must follow their directions.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, you should:

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Wear both the lap belt and the shoulder belt. Using only one part does not protect you well. Even if you have an automatic shoulder belt, buckle your lap belt too.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right turns only.
Right turns permitted.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: Yellow pennant-shaped signs mean no passing zone.

questions.question: If a vehicle is equipped with airbags:

options.text: Seat belts should still be worn.
Seat belts do not need to be worn.
Seat belts should be worn behind the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags are safety devices that help in crashes. For the best protection, always wear your lap and shoulder belts along with airbags.

questions.question: If the roadway is wet or icy, you should:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Drive at the posted speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Wet, snowy, or icy roads make it harder for your tires to grip. Slow down when roads are wet or icy.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce road rage?

options.text: Always signal your intention when changing lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Use your horn frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal your intention when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Follow traffic laws and signals. Always signal before changing lanes to prevent road rage.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You should stop for other traffic.
Traffic is entering from another road and you should allow additional space for drivers to merge safely into the flow of traffic.
Traffic is entering from another road and you should keep right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is entering from another road and you should allow additional space for drivers to merge safely into the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic will merge into your lane. Check your mirrors and move to another lane if possible to give merging drivers room to enter safely.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area designated for road construction workers.
The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are areas where pedestrians cross the road. They are marked with white lines. Some crosswalks are not marked.

questions.question: What is the only medically proven method of removing alcohol or other drug combinations from your system?

options.text: Breathe in some fresh air.
Give your body time.
Drink coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give your body time.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not lower your blood alcohol level. You must wait for your body to process the alcohol.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Stare directly in front of their car.
Only focus on the middle of the road.
Watch beside, ahead, and to the rear of their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch beside, ahead, and to the rear of their car.
questions.explanation: Watch beside, ahead, and behind your car. Know what is happening all around your vehicle.

questions.question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Only when they are in a crosswalk.
Always, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
Only when the traffic light favors them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians near your vehicle at all times. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what the situation is.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner and ready to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your engine until they cross.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.
Wait for the person to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the person to cross.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes, whether the cane has a red tip or not.

questions.question: What should you do before you start the engine?

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: Make a habit of these steps every time you enter and exit your car. Before starting the engine, buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: If you must stop suddenly on an interstate highway, what should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
Get out and flag down the next car that passes.
Pull to the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you stop on the shoulder of an interstate or highway, turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Stay in your vehicle if you can. Standing or walking on an interstate is very dangerous because of the high speed of traffic.

questions.question: When must you obey a school crossing guard?

options.text: At all times.
Only during school hours.
Only when you see children present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Watch for crossing guards near schools and always follow their directions.
